intro: Hey there! I'm going to walk you through Bay Status. It's a simple way for a repair shop to keep customers updated while their car is in the shop. Partway through, you'll get to try it yourself, right from your own phone. Let's jump in.
board: This is the shop board. Every car in the shop is here, sorted by where it is in the repair. Checked in, diagnosing, waiting on the customer's approval, waiting on parts, in progress, quality check, and ready for pickup. Up top, you can see how many cars you have, and how many are waiting on a customer. The orange column is the one to watch, because those customers still need to approve work.
checkin: Let's check in a new car. Sam Ortiz just dropped off his 2014 Mazda CX-5. We put in his name and cell number, the vehicle, and what he's hearing: a squealing belt on cold starts. This box confirms Sam is okay getting texts. Then we check him in.
firsttext: And that's it. Sam just got a text saying we have his car, with a link to follow along. That link is his own page for this car. No app, and no password. Everything we send him shows up here in the message thread, so the whole team can see what was said and when.
estimate: Now let's look at a car that's further along. Lena's Chevy Malibu came in with the A.C. blowing warm. The tech found the problem, so we'll build an estimate. First, an A.C. recharge for 189 dollars. Then, a new condenser for 624.
send: When the estimate is ready, we move the car to approval needed. Bay Status writes the text for you, with the total and the customer's link. You can change the wording if you like. Then we send it.
tryit: Now here's the fun part. Let's try the texting feature. Pretend you're Lena. Enter your cell number below, and we'll text you the same message she would get. Open the link, then approve or decline each repair, just like a customer would. If you'd rather not, tap show me on screen.
waiting: Great, the text is on its way. Open it on your phone, approve or decline each repair, type your name to sign, and send your decision. I'll wait right here.
gotit: Welcome back! Looks like the text worked, and your decision just came through. Back at the shop, the answer shows up right away. You can see exactly what you approved and declined, and your signature with the time. No voicemails, and no, I never said yes to that. Let's keep going and move the car through the rest of the repair.
onscreen: No problem. Here's what Lena sees when she taps the link on her phone. Her car, where it's at in the process, and the estimate. She can approve or decline each repair on its own. Let's say she approves the recharge, but holds off on the condenser for now. She types her name to sign, and sends her decision.
backshop: Back at the shop, her answer shows up right away. You can see exactly what she approved, and her signature with the time. No voicemails, and no, I never said yes to that.
along: From here, you just move the car along as the work happens. In progress. Quality check. Each step can send the customer a quick text, and you decide which ones go out. And when it's done, ready for pickup. The customer gets a text with the total and your hours.
wrap: That's Bay Status. Customers stay in the loop, approvals are signed and saved, and your front desk gets fewer calls. Feel free to keep clicking around this demo shop. It's all sample data, so you can't break anything. Thanks for taking the tour!
